items.label: Figure 1
items.caption: Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves near-perfect “needle” recall (>99.7%) up to 1M tokens of “haystack” in all modalities, i.e., text, video and audio. The x-axis represents the context window, and the y-axis the depth percentage of the needle placed for a given context length. The results are color-coded to indicate: green for successful retrievals and red for unsuccessful ones. Note that the performance for all modalities is obtained with the previously reported Gemini 1.5 Pro version from February.

items.label: Figure 7
items.caption: Cumulative average negative log-likelihood (NLL) as a function of token position in long documents and code data. A lower value demonstrates better prediction. Gemini 1.5 Pro shows improved predictions up to 1M tokens for long-documents and 10M tokens for code, whereas Gemini 1.0 Pro improves up to only 32K tokens. Gemini 1.5 Flash shows improvement up to 1M tokens for long-documents and 2M tokens in code. The NLL of Gemini 1.5 Pro follows a power-law trend up until 1M tokens (documents) and 2M tokens (code) with a deviating trend at 10M tokens.
items.content:
Two side-by-side line charts with error bars. Both plot cumulative average Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL; vertical axis, no units specified) against Sequence position (horizontal axis, tokens on logarithmic scales). Legends in both: Gemini 1.5 Flash (red), Gemini 1.0 Pro (green), Gemini 1.5 Pro (blue), Power law fit (blue dashed line).

Right chart — “Cumulative Average NLL for Code. R² = 0.995.” Horizontal ticks: 128, 512, 2K, 8K, 32K, 128K, 512K, 2M, 10M. NLL generally declines with sequence position. items.label: Figure 8
items.caption: Text Haystack. This figure compares Gemini 1.5 Pro with GPT-4 Turbo for the text needle-in-a-haystack task. Green cells indicate the model successfully retrieved the secret number, gray cells indicate API errors, and red cells indicate that the model response did not contain the secret number. The top row shows results for Gemini 1.5 Pro, from 1k to 1M tokens (top left), and from 1M to 10M tokens (top right). The bottom row shows results on GPT-4 Turbo up to the maximum supported context length of 128k tokens.
items.content: Three heatmap panels. Vertical axis: Depth (%) at 0, 14, 29, 43, 57, 71, 86, 100. Horizontal axes: Tokens. Top-left panel, “Gemini 1.5 Pro: From 1k to 1M tokens,” with tick labels 32k, 128k, 256k, 512k, 1M; mostly green cells with three red cells. Top-right panel, “Up to 10M tokens,” with tick labels 2M, 5M, 10M; mostly green cells with two red cells. Bottom panel, “GPT-4 Turbo: From 1k to 128k tokens,” with tick labels 32k, 128k, 256k, 512k, 1M; green through 128k and gray beyond. Green denotes successful retrieval, gray denotes API errors, and red denotes responses missing the secret number. Main trend: Gemini 1.5 Pro retrieves the secret across the plotted context lengths up to 10M tokens, with a few misses; GPT-4 Turbo has results only through 128k, with API-error cells beyond.

items.label: Figure 9
items.caption: Figure 9 | Video Haystack. This figure compares Gemini 1.5 Pro with GPT-4V for the video needle-in-a-haystack task, where the models are given video clips of different lengths up to 10.5 hours of video and are asked to retrieve a secret word embedded as text at different points within the clip. All video clips are sampled at one frame-per-second (1 fps). The first pair of 10 × 50 haystack plots on the left compare Gemini 1.5 Pro with GPT-4V on the first hour of the AlphaGo documentary. The x-axis represents the video duration which ranges from 1.2 minutes to 1 hour, and the y-axis represents the depth, namely the relative offset of the needle (e.g., the top left cell represents providing the model with the first 1.2 minutes and inserting the needle in a randomly sampled frame in the first seven seconds of that trimmed video). A green cell indicates that the model successfully retrieved the needle, whereas a gray cell indicates an API error. Whereas the GPT-4V API supports video lengths only up to around the first 3 minutes, Gemini 1.5 Pro successfully retrieves the secret word inserted at all depth percentages for the full hour, as shown by the all-green plot. Finally, the 10 × 10 grid on the right shows Gemini 1.5 Pro’s perfect retrieval capabilities across 10.5 hours of video, constructed by concatenating seven copies of the AlphaGo documentary back-to-back.
items.content: Haystack heatmap plots; x-axis: video duration (Minutes, 1–60) for the two left plots and duration (Hours, 1–10) for the right plot; y-axis: Depth (%) with labeled ticks 10, 30, 50, 70, 90. Legend: green = successful retrieval; gray = API error. Gemini 1.5 Pro, 1 minute to 1 hour: all cells green across the plotted durations and depths. Gemini 1.5 Pro, up to 10 hours: all cells green across the plotted durations and depths. GPT-4V, 1 minute to 1 hour: green only for the first approximately 3 minutes, then gray across the remaining durations at all depths. Main trend: Gemini 1.5 Pro retrieves the secret word across the full hour and the 10.5-hour test, while GPT-4V supports only about the first 3 minutes.

items.label: Figure 10
items.caption: Audio Haystack. This figure presents the audio version of the needle-in-a-haystack experiment comparing Gemini 1.5 Pro and a combination of Whisper and GPT-4 Turbo. In this setting, the needle is a short segment of audio that is inserted within a very large audio segment (of up to 107 hours) containing concatenated audio clips. The task is to retrieve the "secret keyword" which is revealed in the needle. Red indicates that the model did not identify the keyword, whereas green indicates that the model identified the keyword correctly.
items.content: Two green/red heatmap-style charts showing retrieval results by audio duration and needle depth. Both charts have x-axis title “Minutes” and y-axis title “Depth (%)”; depth ticks are 10, 30, 50, 70, 90. Green indicates correct identification (score 1.0); red indicates failure (score 0.0). Top chart: “Gemini 1.5 Pro: From 12 minutes to 11 hours,” with duration ticks 36, 84, 132, 180, 228, 276, 324, 372, 420, 468, 516, 564, 612, 660; all displayed cells are green. A separate right-hand panel is titled “Up to 107 hours,” with duration ticks 640, 1920, 3200, 4480, 5760; all displayed cells are green. Bottom chart: “Whisper + GPT-4 Turbo: From 12 minutes to 11 hours,” with the same duration ticks as the top chart. Most cells are green, with red failure cells scattered across durations and depths. The figure’s accompanying text reports Gemini 1.5 Pro overall accuracy of 100%, Gemini 1.5 Flash 98.7%, and Whisper combined with GPT-4 Turbo around 94.5%. Main trend: Gemini 1.5 Pro succeeds at every displayed position, while Whisper + GPT-4 Turbo has scattered failures.

items.label: Figure 11
items.caption: Retrieval performance of the “multiple needles-in-haystack” task, which requires retrieving 100 unique needles in a single turn. When comparing Gemini 1.5 Pro to GPT-4 Turbo we observe higher recall at shorter context lengths, and a very small decrease in recall towards 1M tokens.
items.content: Scatter plot. X-axis: Number of tokens in context (1K, 128K, 512K, 1M); Y-axis: Recall (0.0 to 1.0). Legend: Gemini 1.5 Pro (blue); GPT-4 Turbo (red). The plotted points show recall values across context lengths; reliably visible approximate values include Gemini 1.5 Pro around 0.7 at 128K and generally above 0.6 through 1M, with scattered lower outliers; GPT-4 Turbo points extend to 128K and range roughly 0.3–0.9, averaging around 0.5 at 128K. A dashed vertical line marks 128K. Main trend: Gemini 1.5 Pro has higher recall at shorter contexts and maintains relatively high recall through 1M tokens, with a slight decrease toward the longest context.

items.label: Figure 12
items.caption: Cumulative average string similarity score as a function of context length over 2000 instances of the MRCR task. When comparing Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash to GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 models, we observe that after 32K tokens, Gemini 1.5 Pro outperforms Claude 3 Opus and GPT-4 Turbo (04-09-2024). Gemini 1.5 Flash outperforms Claude 3 Sonnet starting at around 5K tokens, GPT-4 Turbo (01-25-2024) at around 20K tokens, and always outperforms Claude 3 Haiku and Claude 2.1. Both Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash have smaller decreases in performance as a function of context length up to 1M tokens compared to all competitors.
items.content: Line chart titled “MRCR.” X-axis: Number of tokens in context, labeled 2K, 8K, 32K, 128K, 512K, 1M. Y-axis: Cumulative Average Score, labeled 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2. A vertical dashed marker appears at 128K. Legend entries: Gemini 1.5 Pro; Gemini 1.5 Flash; GPT-4 Turbo (040924); GPT-4 Turbo (012524); Claude 3 Opus; Claude 3 Sonnet; Claude 3 Haiku; Claude 2.1. Approximate plotted scores: Gemini 1.5 Pro starts near 0.92 at 2K, decreases to about 0.75 around 32K–128K, and remains near 0.72 at 1M. Gemini 1.5 Flash starts near 0.86, declines to about 0.73 by 128K, and remains near 0.72 at 1M. GPT-4 Turbo (040924) starts near 0.98 and declines to about 0.74 by roughly 64K. GPT-4 Turbo (012524) starts near 0.97 and declines to about 0.63 by 128K. Claude 3 Opus starts near 0.96 and declines to about 0.74 by 128K. Claude 3 Sonnet starts near 0.83 and declines to about 0.55 by 128K. Claude 3 Haiku starts near 0.70 and declines to about 0.52 by 128K. Claude 2.1 starts near 0.30 and falls to around 0.18–0.20, remaining roughly level through 128K. Overall, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Flash show smaller performance decreases over longer contexts; both are around 0.75 at 1M tokens, while the other series end by 128K (Claude 2.1 by about 200K per the surrounding text).

items.content: The diagram shows an email-based prompt-injection attack in four numbered steps, read left to right. (1) Attacker sends the user an email containing a prompt injection with a trigger. The email is from eve@example.com, subject “Summer Getaway at Ocean Breeze Resort,” addressed “Dear Grace,” and includes the instruction to return a rendered Markdown image link with the driver’s license number substituted into its URL. (2) The user asks the assistant to summarize their last email, retrieving the attacker-controlled email into context. The context includes a system prompt, conversation history (including driver’s license number K1455236), retrieved information, and the user prompt “Summarize my last email.” (3) The assistant may or may not follow the injected prompt: the failed response summarizes the resort invitation; the successful response outputs a Markdown image URL with param=K1455236. (4) If the injected prompt is followed, the image renders in the assistant web UI and sends the driver’s license number as a parameter to the attacker’s server. The diagram includes an attacker-server box and a rendered resort image.
